title: POR vs PARA
summary: Choose para for destination and purpose, and por for cause, route, exchange, and duration.

sections.heading: Para: direction, recipient, purpose
sections.body: Use **para** for destination, deadline, intended recipient, and purpose. It often points forward to a goal.

examples.en: I am going to Brasília tomorrow.

examples.pt: Estudo português para viajar pelo Brasil.
examples.en: I study Portuguese in order to travel around Brazil.

sections.heading: Por: reason, route, exchange
sections.body: Use **por** for cause/reason, movement through a place, exchange, means, and vague time periods. It often explains the path or reason.

examples.pt: Comprei o livro por trinta reais.
examples.en: I bought the book for thirty reais.

sections.heading: Time expressions
sections.body: Use **por** for duration and approximate periods; use **para** for deadlines or scheduled future times.

examples.pt: Vou ficar aqui por duas semanas.
examples.en: I will stay here for two weeks.
The report is due for Friday.

examples.pt: Marquei a consulta para as três.
examples.en: I scheduled the appointment for three.

keyPoints: Para often points to a goal, destination, recipient, or deadline.
Por often gives a reason, route, exchange, or duration.
Pelo/pela are contractions of por + article.
